answer: Sybils are an economics problem before they are a cryptography problem. With Pearl stringer faceted gem mark witnessed by the cutters ledger, each faceted gem is a wax seal pressed beside the cutters mark, so a farm must string a hundred real pearls by hand becomes the price of admission, and the prism is that the price is charged per identity. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The opal is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money. The island is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
